title: SIF Minimum Investment Rule: How the ₹10 Lakh Threshold is Calculated
description: Specified Investment Funds (SIFs) require a minimum investment of ₹10 lakhs per investor. This ₹10 lakh threshold is calculated at the investor's Permanent Ac.

faq.q: What exactly is a Specified Investment Fund (SIF)?
faq.a: A Specified Investment Fund (SIF) is a category of mutual fund schemes that often have specific investment mandates or cater to a particular class of investors. They are typically subject to a higher minimum investment threshold, like the ₹10 lakh rule, as per regulatory guidelines.

faq.q: Does the ₹10 lakh minimum apply to all mutual funds?
faq.a: No, the ₹10 lakh minimum investment rule specifically applies to Specified Investment Funds (SIFs), not to all mutual funds. Most regular equity, debt, or hybrid mutual fund schemes have much lower minimum investment requirements, often starting from ₹500 for SIPs.

faq.q: What happens if my SIF investment value drops below ₹10 lakhs due to market conditions?
faq.a: While market-driven depreciation below ₹10 lakhs might not immediately trigger a forced liquidation, the fund house reserves the right to take action if the investment consistently remains below the threshold. The primary concern for breach is usually investor-initiated withdrawals.

faq.q: Can I combine SIF investments from different AMCs to meet the ₹10 lakh threshold?
faq.a: No, the ₹10 lakh threshold is calculated at the PAN level *within a single Asset Management Company (AMC)*. You cannot combine investments made in SIFs from different fund houses to meet this aggregate minimum.

faq.q: What if I'm investing through an SIP and haven't reached ₹10 lakhs yet?
faq.a: If you are investing through an SIP, your cumulative investment contributes to the threshold. However, some AMCs might require an initial lump sum or a commitment to reach the ₹10 lakh mark within a stipulated timeframe. It's best to check with your AMC for their specific policy.

faq.q: Is there a penalty for breaching the ₹10 lakh minimum?
faq.a: While there isn't a direct "penalty" fee, the consequence of breaching the minimum is that the fund house may liquidate your remaining units in the SIF. This ensures they remain compliant with the regulatory requirements for SIFs.
